name: Soudan 2
notes: Placement: the surveyed point of the MINOS far-detector cavern is used as an approximate stand-in for the Soudan mine's 27th-level experimental area; no source read gives the Soudan 2 cavern's own position, and the two detectors did not operate together (Soudan 2 1989-2001, MINOS far detector 2003-2016).

physics_goals.quote: Soudan 2 was originally designed to study proton decay
physics_goals.value: Search for nucleon decay (the original design goal); atmospheric-neutrino flavour ratio and oscillations were studied with the same data

summary.plain: A 963-ton iron-and-gas detector, 700 metres down in a Minnesota iron mine, built to search for protons decaying. From 1989 to 2001 it set proton-decay lifetime limits above 10^32 years for some decay modes, and recorded atmospheric neutrinos well enough to see the signature of muon-neutrino oscillation.
summary.technical: Iron tracking calorimeter with honeycomb geometry operating as a time projection chamber (224 modules of 4.3 t, 963 t total, 770 t fiducial) at 2070 m.w.e., surrounded by an active shield. Nucleon-decay searches (e.g. lepton + K0 modes: tau/B > 1.5e32 yr for p to mu+ K0s) and atmospheric-neutrino analyses: flavour ratio 0.64 +- 0.11 +- 0.06 of expectation (3.9 kt-yr), oscillations observed in 5.90 fiducial kt-yr.
